newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Gemex says to buy Agral debt free.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Gemex says to buy Agral debt free.

text.p: The head of Grupo Embotellador de Mexico (Gemex) said on Tuesday his firm would only buy Grupo Protexa's Agral bottling unit once it has been freed of some $72 million of debt by Pepsico Inc.
Protexa said on Tuesday it had agreed to sell Agral to Pepsico and Gemex, but Gemex, which is Pepsico's anchor bottler in Mexico, said its part of the deal was not yet completed.
"We are planning to buy a company without debt," Gemex chairman Enrique Molina told Reuters. "Pepsico has to negotiate (Agral's) debt first."
He said Gemex believed Agral, freed of its debts, was worth $35-40 million, and that would be paid to Pepsico when the debts were cancelled.

Before the latest deal, Pepsico owned a 49 percent stake in Agral, the franchise bottler for Mexico's third city of Monterrey. Protexa is one of Mexico's largest privately held firms, with interests mainly in construction and engineering.
Gemex's B shares headed gainers in the Mexican bolsa on Tuesday, climbing 23.08 percent to 3.20 pesos. Its CPOs were up 6.94 percent at 12.94 pesos.
